## Dengue data

To predict dengue status, you build a model that uses Age, WBC, and PLT as explanatory variables. You fit the model in R, and compute the deviance on the training data:

```{r echo=F}
library(glmhelpR)
```

```{r}
m_dengue1 <- glm(Dengue ~ Age + WBC + PLT, 
                      data = dengue, 
                      family = binomial)
m_dengue1$deviance
```

Your friend also builds a model, but they also include HCT in their model:


```{r}
m_dengue2 <- glm(Dengue ~ Age + WBC + PLT + HCT,
                 data = dengue, family = binomial)
m_dengue2$deviance
```

### Question

1. Your friend notices that their model has a smaller deviance, and so they argue that their model is preferable to yours. What do you think?
